title: The dovetail mate
summary: A protected queen right next to the king, on a diagonal, mates when the king's own pieces block the squares behind it.

steps.title: The dovetail shape
steps.text: A queen on d6 would sit diagonally next to Black's king, protected by the pawn on e5. From there she covers every square around the king except two: e8 and f7. Both are filled by Black's own rook and pawn. The shape of the queen and the two blocked squares looks like the tail of a dove, which gives the mate its name.
steps.narration: Here's a sneaky one. If your queen lands right next to the king on a diagonal, and something protects her, she covers almost every square. The two squares she misses, e8 and f7, are blocked by Black's own pieces.

steps.title: Land the queen
steps.hint: Your pawn on e5 protects one square diagonally next to the king.
steps.success: Queen to d6 is mate. The pawn on e5 protects her, she covers d7, d8, e6, f6 and f8, and Black's rook and pawn block e8 and f7.
steps.narration: Your move. Slide the queen up the d-file to d6. The pawn protects her, and Black's own rook and pawn do the rest.

steps.title: Drive the king into the dovetail
steps.prompt: Mate in two. Check with the bishop first.
steps.hint: The bishop can check from h6. If the king steps to e7, the queen has a square next to it.
steps.success: Bishop to h6 check pushes the king to e7, and queen to d6 is the dovetail mate.
steps.narration: Start with a bishop check from h6. The king walks out to e7, right into the dovetail, and your queen lands on d6 for mate.

steps.title: What makes it mate?
steps.question: In the dovetail mate, what stops the king from escaping to the two squares the queen does not cover?

options.text: The king's own pieces stand on them
options.why: The queen covers everything else. The defender's own pieces close the last two doors.

options.text: The queen covers them from a distance
options.why: From a diagonal next to the king, the queen misses two squares. Something else has to fill them.

options.text: The pawn protecting the queen covers them
options.why: That pawn's job is to protect the queen so the king cannot take her.

steps.narration: Last question. The queen misses two squares in this mate. What closes them? Answer this, and you've finished the mating patterns. Wonderful work!
